answer:
## Answer (hypothesis)

**Between 3400 and 3000 BCE the number of monuments and the number of axes/celts do not track the elements of symbolic capital.** Monument Count (`MonumentCount`/`ZMonument`) and Axes/Celts (`AxesCelts`/`ZBeil`) rise and fall *together* as a single shared maximum in the 3200–3100 BCE bins (r = **+0.87**, exact permutation p = 0.074), and their only strong in-window companion is **Depot** — hoards, i.e. economic capital (r = **+0.85** for monuments, **+0.93** for axes/celts, p = 0.074 / 0.041). Symbolic capital contributes nothing contemporaneously: **Daggers** are constant (Z = −0.58 all five bins) and **Hatchets&Swords** vary by 0.01 Z (SD 0.004), so both carry *no* in-window signal (reported as undefined, not r = 0); **House Size**, the only symbolic element with range, **falls** from its EN/MN maximum (+2.05 at 3400 BCE) to ≈0 while monuments/axes rise. Levels therefore give a **weak negative** target~symbolic association (MonumentCount r = **−0.35**, ρ = −0.41, p = 0.60; AxesCelts r = **−0.17**, ρ = −0.37, p = 0.74), and the composite symbolic-capital index gives exactly the same numbers because it **is** House Size (r = 1.000 with House Size by construction — two of three elements enter as a constant 0). In the **changes** view (reported separately, never pooled): MonumentCount~ΔHouse Size r = **−0.04** (p = 0.96) versus AxesCelts~ΔHouse Size r = **+0.50** (p = 0.56, LOAO 0.28…0.72, sign agreement 2/2) — so levels and changes are not interchangeable even here.

Crucially, the negative level relation is a **boundary artefact**: dropping the 3400 BCE bin (MN-only core, N = 4) flips both signs (MonumentCount −0.35 → **+0.27**; AxesCelts −0.17 → **+0.37**), and House Size's step sits precisely on the EN→MN transition (−1.35 at 3600 → +2.05 at 3500/3400). Out-of-window context (3800–2800 BCE, 11 bins, **labelled context, not window evidence**) shows symbolic capital *leading* rather than co-varying: House Size vs Monument Count r = +0.15 at lag 0 but **+0.68 at +2 bins (200 yr)**; vs Axes/Celts +0.14 → **+0.56**. So the defensible hypothesis is that in 3400–3000 BCE monuments and axes/celts are driven by depositional/economic activity and demography, with house-size-based symbolic capital acting as a **lagged (~2 centuries) precursor** outside the window, not as a contemporaneous driver inside it.

## Key evidence (executed; all exact label-permutation p, no asymptotic p, no inference on yearly `_inter` grids)

In-window anchor grid (Z, chronological; KDE ×10⁴ / growth ×10³):

| BCE | MonumentCount | AxesCelts | HouseSize | HatchetSword | Dagger | Depot | MonumentSize | CopperGold | openness | group |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|3400|−0.465|0.37|2.05|−0.43|−0.58|−0.45|0.409|0.69|1.645|MN|
|3300|−0.133|0.32|0.79|−0.43|−0.58|−0.43|0.427|−0.50|2.095|MN|
|3200|**0.913**|**2.60**|0.79|−0.43|−0.58|**−0.29**|−0.202|−0.60|0.747|MN|
|3100|0.352|0.80|−0.06|−0.42|−0.58|−0.37|0.678|−0.60|0.330|MN|
|3000|−0.363|0.80|0.19|−0.43|−0.58|−0.37|−0.217|−0.60|−1.157|MN|

Levels table (r / exact perm p): House Size −0.352 (0.603) and −0.166 (0.736); Pottery Form −0.194/−0.291; Pottery Decoration −0.172/−0.276; Copper/Gold −0.538 (ρ −0.671, p 0.306)/−0.401 (ρ −0.803, p 0.207); Depot +0.852 (0.074)/**+0.930 (0.041)**; Monument Size −0.195/−0.619 (0.273); HatchetSword, Dagger, Amber, Sickle = undefined. LOAO ranges straddle 0 for every symbolic pair (e.g. −0.678…+0.270 for monuments~House Size). Interval sign agreement is 1/3 and 2/2.

Covariates: openness↔MonumentCount −0.02, ↔AxesCelts −0.22, ↔House Size **+0.63** (SMOOTH_MEAN_100y: −0.07/−0.25/+0.68). Partial r(target~House Size | openness): −0.441 (p 0.455) and −0.039 (0.901); | `kde_all_mean`: −0.172/​+0.367; | `g_all_mean`: −0.525/−0.155 — nothing survives covariate adjustment at N = 5. Observation-effort check matters: **House Size correlates r = +0.93 with `kde_all_mean`** in-window, so part of its trajectory is dating density, and openness declines monotonically (2.10 → −1.16) across the window.

Symbolic capital is **not distinctive**: the largest coefficients in the whole grid belong to Depot and to the two targets against each other; every symbolic-cell p > 0.5. One cell (Depot×AxesCelts p = 0.041) is economic capital, not symbolic, and is unremarkable as the minimum of ~48 tests (minimum attainable exact p with N = 5 is 0.008).

Robustness/verification: independently re-derived r and permutation p for four pairs (MC–HS −0.352, AX–HS −0.166, AX–DE 0.930 with p = 0.041, MC–AX 0.868) and LOAO range (−0.678…+0.270) — all reproduce the script output. `capital.csv` ≡ `time_series_data.csv` to 0.0e+00 on all 12 paired columns, so no reconciliation risk; pollen `Belau_PC1_inter` ≡ `pollen_inter` within the window (max|diff| 4e-15).

## Limitations
N = 5 bins (N = 4 for changes; minimum attainable two-sided exact p = 0.008 / 0.040); two of three symbolic-capital elements are information-free in-window and the composite is therefore a House-Size relabelling; the 3400 BCE EN/MN boundary bin controls the sign of every symbolic association; Amber (range 0.08 Z), HatchetSword (0.01 Z) and Depot (0.16 Z) vary on the scale of the published 2-decimal quantisation, so small-r cells are rounding-sensitive; a single nominal p < 0.05 among ~48 tests is expected by chance; extended-window lag results (3800–2800 BCE) are context only and include the EN period, so they cannot be quoted as window evidence; `pollen_grate_100` was ignored because it does not match its documented formula.

payload.hypothesis: Between 3400 and 3000 BCE the number of monuments (MonumentCount/ZMonument) and of axes & celts (AxesCelts/ZBeil) is not positively driven by contemporary symbolic capital. The two targets move together as one peak in the 3200-3100 BCE bins (r=+0.87, exact permutation p=0.074) and their strongest companion is Depot/hoards, i.e. economic capital (r=+0.85 monuments, +0.93 axes/celts). Symbolic-capital elements add nothing contemporaneously: Daggers (ZDolch) are constant (Z=-0.58) and Hatchets&Swords (ZAxtSchwert) vary by 0.01 Z, so both carry no in-window signal, and House Size (Zhausgr) declines from its EN/MN maximum (+2.05 at 3400 BCE) to ~0, giving weak negative level associations (MonumentCount r=-0.35, p=0.60; AxesCelts r=-0.17, p=0.74; composite index identical to House Size, r=1.000) that reverse for Axes/Celts in the changes view (r=+0.50) and flip sign when the 3400 BCE EN/MN boundary bin is dropped (to +0.27 and +0.37). Pollen openness (Belau_PC1) is essentially unrelated to the targets (r=-0.02 and -0.22) but tracks House Size (r=+0.63), and House Size also tracks observation effort (r=+0.93 with kde_all_mean), so covariation involving House Size is demographic/sampling rather than symbolic. Hypothesis: in 3400-3000 BCE monuments and axes/celts are governed by depositional/economic activity and population dynamics, while house-size symbolic capital acts as a lagged precursor (~200 years) visible only in the wider 3800-2800 BCE context (r=+0.68 monuments, +0.56 axes/celts at +2 bins) - all statements conditional on N=5 one-century bins, for which no association is statistically decisive.
payload.workflow: Read-only inspection -> anchor grid extraction (100-yr bins, 5 anchors 3400-3000 BCE, CE=-BCE, calBP=1950-BCE, time_series authoritative) -> verified capital.csv == time_series_data.csv on all 12 paired Z columns (max|diff| 0.0) and Belau_PC1_inter == pollen_inter in-window -> per-target x per-predictor Pearson and tie-corrected Spearman with exhaustive 5! label-permutation two-sided p, leave-one-anchor-out ranges and interval sign agreement, for levels and for 100-yr changes separately -> composite symbolic-capital index from within-window z-scores (flat elements contribute 0) with dominance explicitly reported -> covariate checks: Belau openness (raw, 100-yr smoothed, recomputed 100-yr growth) and observation effort (kde_all_mean, g_all_mean) with partial correlations -> EN/MN 3400 BCE boundary sensitivity -> extended 3800-2800 BCE (11 anchors) cross-correlation at lags -2..+2 bins used only as labelled context. Flat/near-flat series reported as undefined, never as r=0; no asymptotic p-values; no inference on the yearly linear-interpolated grids.
